A Student-Led Project

Compassion Driven Change

We're students who believe that Compassion should be accompanied by effective Action to drive real Change. We do this in practical ways, by turning everyday things some people want to get rid of and others need — such as spare coins, lightly used items like toys, electronics, books, and digital products — into cash for our cause. To this we add our secret sauces — Compassion, Creativity, and Collaboration (with a big helping of Grit) to bring much-needed help for the innocent children whose lives have been turned upside down by the trauma of war and other forms of violence. We value and enable small acts of compassion that can be carried out by anyone, regardless of means. Yet to a child in need, our impact can be big, even life altering. This is why our slogan is “small change for big change.”

Our Story

It all started with a jar of coins.

When the bombs started falling in Ukraine in 2022, I was a 12-year-old kid watching other kids lose their homes, their schools, and sometimes their lives for no fault of their own. I felt powerless, as I couldn't fly overseas to help — but it occurred to me that I could collect the loose change that had piled up in my garage over a decade, convert it to currency, get my parents to make a matching contribution, and send the funds to an organization that can change the life of a child in Ukraine. My friend Guntas and I did this for two years, in our schools and neighborhoods. That simple idea won the Best Social Enterprise Award at the 2024 annual gala of The Indus Entrepreneurs (TiE), New Jersey Chapter, and became the driving force behind Children of War Project.

Today we're a student-led team of changemakers on a simple mission: make it easy, fun, and meaningful for young people to help children affected by war, homelessness, and poverty. We collect coins, run garage and online sales, resell used books, and we're creating digital storybooks — to gather small sums of money. We call this "Small Change for BIG Change," and every penny counts. Please join our movement!

"In the summer of 2018, when I was visiting Kochi, India, the power went off due to the heavy rains. That night as the flood waters rose, my grandma held my hand and told me that to be useful, instead of cursing the darkness, light a lamp. She then showed me how. It is this spirit of finding a way to be helpful by doing something which gave birth to the CoW project. We are the lamp!"— Yuvraaj Kumar (Yuvi), Founder & President

Board of Trustees & Advisors

Experienced mentors and community leaders guiding CoW's mission and stewardship.

Wesley Mathews

Brings over two decades of experience in economic development, diplomacy, and finance to his role as Vice President, State Government Affairs, PSEG. He was previously President & CEO of Choose New Jersey, the State’s leading nonprofit business-attraction organization. Before that, he was a career diplomat in the U.S. Foreign Service, serving at embassies and consulates in Saudi Arabia, India, Pakistan, Germany, and Nigeria, as well as at the State Department in Washington, D.C. He is Chair of the New Jersey–India Commission and serves on several boards, including the President’s Leadership Council at Stevens Institute of Technology and the FIFA World Cup 2026 New York New Jersey Host Committee.

Lata Setty

An attorney turned serial founder of companies backed by VCs including Sequoia Capital and Goldman Sachs, and the inaugural investor at How Women Invest Funds I, II, and III — an early-stage venture firm with a portfolio of 35+ companies. She serves on the boards of multiple high-impact startups and non-profits, including The Indus Entrepreneurs (TiE), NJ Chapter. Through How Women Invest she helped launch “The New Table,” an initiative to mobilize 10,000 women to invest in venture capital by 2027, and rang the NASDAQ opening bell to mark the launch of its $100 million Fund III. She was recently named Global Business Woman of the Year at the British Parliament in London.

Prema Roddam

An attorney specializing in global mobility, workforce management, corporate immigration, and related compliance and advisory services, with experience spanning Telecom, IT, Healthcare, Pharma, and Entertainment. She has worked extensively with leading non-profits — including Manavi, Akshaya Patra, the South Asian Bar Association, and The Indus Entrepreneurs (TiE), NJ — supporting their governance and continuing compliance. She has been recognized by NJBIZ as a Leader in Law and an NJ ROI Influencer in Law.

Dr. Thomas Abraham

Founder, President, and Chairman of the Global Organization for People of Indian Origin (GOPIO). He convened the First Global Convention of People of Indian Origin in New York, where GOPIO was formed, and previously served as executive trustee of the GOPIO Foundation. Dr. Abraham is also President of Innovative Research and Products, Inc. (Stamford, CT), a multi-client market-research firm in next-generation technologies — advanced materials, nanotechnology, electronic components, and energy generation and storage.

How We Work

From a jar of coins → to a child in need

Here's exactly how your spare change becomes real help — and where every dollar goes.

1📣

It starts with outreach & awareness

We create awareness and raise funds by collecting spare coins, garage & online sales of lightly used items, and the design and sale of illustrated storybooks and technical services such as websites, voice assistants, and AI agents — every bit feeds the cause.

↓
2🤝

Student ambassadors sell & fundraise

Our student ambassadors lead the sales, drives, and community outreach.

↓
3❤️

CoW pools every dollar and finds matching donors 100% of net proceeds

All the small amounts add up into one meaningful gift for children.

↓
4💵

Donated to trusted child-welfare groups

Vetted child-welfare organizations worldwide, selected by our Board of Trustees and Advisors.

↓
5📊

You get an annual report

We send you a yearly report showing exactly how every dollar was spent.

Join the Movement

Join the Movement

Want to make a real difference and learn something amazing about how to build an impactful non-profit that helps children in need? Join CoW at the level that's right for you, then start a coin drive at your school, run a book sale, and lead your own mini-campaign — we'll give you everything you need.

Level 1🤝 Volunteer
Volunteer or donate items · no contribution needed
  • Free CoW-branded Coin Jar (welcome gift for everyone)
  • Starter kit: flyers, tips & a community of student changemakers
  • Volunteer / service hours
Level 2🌱 Supporter
Volunteer, donate, or raise $100
  • Everything above, plus a digital certificate of appreciation.
Level 3⭐ Activist
Volunteer, donate, or raise $250
  • Everything above, plus lead your own mini-campaign with CoW support and a spot on our Change Maker Wall.
Level 4🏆 Ambassador
Volunteer, donate, or raise $500
  • Everything above, plus a leadership role, a service-hours letter, and a spotlight feature.
Level 5🪔 Change Maker
Volunteer, donate, or raise $1,000
  • Everything above, plus:
  • Mentoring sessions with the CoW founders
  • A personalized letter of recommendation for college applications
  • A free copy of the book The Founders Compass
